brewing.notes: A common starting point for herbal infusions: boiling water, about five minutes.

description:
A liangcha made from the stems and leaves of Taxillus chinensis, drunk mainly in Guangdong and Hong Kong. The version from Wuzhou in Guangxi is the best known.

Brew it as you would other herbal infusions. If the plant is new to you, check that it is safe for you first, especially when pregnant or on medication.
history: The plant is recorded as a medicine in the Shengcao Yaoxing Beiyao of the late Kangxi era, and Xie Qikun's Guangxi Tongzhi notes it as a drink already well regarded in Wuzhou. Its traditional health claims have no medical proof. Little more is documented.
processing: The stems and leaves are simmered with other ingredients, or decocted and dried for steeping; a sweet version is cooked with red dates, eggs or quail eggs and rock sugar.
harvest_season: Gathered all year, though autumn and winter are said to be best.
appearance_liquor: Depends on the plant; usually pale to amber.
taste_profile: A herbal infusion; the taste depends on the plant.
vintage_note: Herbal infusions are not sold by vintage: buy recent stock and use it within a year or so.
